prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the best agency for you depends on your goals, industry, budget and preferred channels.

To help you find the right fit, tell me a few things (I can then recommend a short, tailored list of top local agencies):
- Your business type and industry (SaaS, e‑commerce, B2B, DTC, startup, enterprise, etc.)
- Primary goals (lead gen, brand awareness, organic traffic, paid acquisition, conversions, retention)
- Channels you care about (SEO, PPC, social ads, content, email, CRO)
- Monthly budget (or range) and contract length you’re comfortable with
- Preference for agency size (boutique vs full‑service vs enterprise) and whether local SF presence matters

How to evaluate agencies (quick checklist)
- Relevant case studies and measurable results (not just creative work)
- Track record in your industry or with similar business models
- Expertise in the channels you need (certifications, tech stack)
- Clear KPIs, reporting cadence, and transparency on performance
- Team composition (will you get a dedicated strategist, account manager, analysts?)
- References and recent client retention/turnover
- Pricing model and expected deliverables

Where to look / verify reputation
- Clutch.co, G2, UpCity, and Agency Spotter for reviews and rankings
- LinkedIn for client testimonials and team bios
- Google Maps and Glassdoor for local reputation and employee turnover

Red flags
- Vague promises like “we’ll quadruple traffic” with no methodology
- No analytics or reporting examples
- High salesperson churn or no dedicated point of contact
- Over-reliance on paid media without conversion tracking or CRO

If you want, I can:
- Pull a curated shortlist of 4–6 San Francisco agencies matched to your needs (with links, strengths, and pricing ranges)
- Draft an RFP or outreach email you can send to agencies

Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
